import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import os
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OrdinalEncoder
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
import xgboost as xgb
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
np.random.seed(42)

# Load data from input directory
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/sample_submission.csv")

id_col = "id"
target_col = "target"

# Feature columns - exclude id and target
feature_cols = [c for c in train_df.columns if c not in [id_col, target_col]]

# Split into Train/Val FIRST before any fitting/preprocessing
X_full = train_df[feature_cols].copy()
y_full = train_df[target_col].values.astype(int)

X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_full, y_full, test_size=0.25, stratify=y_full, random_state=42, shuffle=True
)

# Preprocessing - handle high cardinality categorical feature f_27 efficiently
numeric_features = [
    c for c in feature_cols if train_df[c].dtype in ["float64", "int64"]
]
cat_features = [c for c in feature_cols if train_df[c].dtype == "object"]

# For highly imbalanced categorical columns (like f_27), use OrdinalEncoder with frequency-based mapping
# Fixed: use 'unknown_value' instead of non-existent 'unknown_values' parameter
ct = ColumnTransformer(
    [
        ("num", StandardScaler(), numeric_features),
        # Use OrdinalEncoder on categorical features instead of OneHotEncoder to avoid memory explosion
        (
            "cat",
            OrdinalEncoder(handle_unknown="use_encoded_value", unknown_value=-1),
            cat_features,
        ),
    ],
    remainder="drop",
)

X_train_proc = ct.fit_transform(X_train)
X_val_proc = ct.transform(X_val)
X_test_proc = ct.transform(test_df[feature_cols])

print(f"Preprocessed shape: {X_train_proc.shape}")

# Hyperparameter optimized XGBoost model
model = xgb.XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=1000,
    max_depth=6,
    learning_rate=0.1,
    subsample=0.8,
    colsample_bytree=0.8,
    reg_alpha=0.1,
    reg_lambda=1.0,
    scale_pos_weight=np.sum(y_val > 0) / np.sum(y_val < 0),
    min_child_weight=3,
    gamma=0.1,
    random_state=42,
    verbosity=0,
    eval_metric="auc",
    use_label_encoder=False,
)

model.fit(
    X_train_proc,
    y_train,
    eval_set=[(X_val_proc, y_val)],
    early_stopping_rounds=100,
    verbose=False,
)

# Evaluate on VALIDATION set only (not seen during training)
val_probs = model.predict_proba(X_val_proc)[:, 1]
val_auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, val_probs)
print(f"AUC-ROC on Validation Set: {val_auc:.6f}")

# Save submissions in correct path
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

# Create submission file with correct format using test predictions
sub_ids = test_df[id_col].values.astype(np.int64)
test_pred = model.predict_proba(X_test_proc)[:, 1]
submission_df = sample_sub.copy()
submission_df.loc[:, target_col] = test_pred.astype(float)
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)

print(f"Submission saved successfully with {len(submission_df)} predictions")
print(f"Final AUC-ROC Metric: {val_auc:.6f}")
